items.headline: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after affair with alleged spy as Trump says 'I made the deal'
items.blurb: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
items.text: Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The company had come under pressure from Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to reverse course and bring Huang back. But Democrats have accused the Trump administration of selling out national security for financial gain. Huang is due to testify before Congress in early December. His comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that had left the S&P 500 in correction territory. Stock prices for Nvidia fell sharply after Huang stepped down, but jumped by 31% after he was reappointed on Monday - adding about $1tn to the company's market value. Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”. “We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia’s aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” the Ukrainian president added. Zelenskyy released video footage, filmed by an approaching drone, showing the drones as they smashed into the side of the warship at its berth in the Benghazi naval base, triggering huge explosions that lit up the night sky. items.text: The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America. The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US. The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang. The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China. When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed. Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang. items.headline: UN chief calls for world to agree on AI oversight within a year
items.blurb: Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has become increasingly vocal about AI as end of term nears.
items.text: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for measures to better manage the risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) during a conference in Barbados. “Today I call for member states to coordinate efforts and to develop within the next year a globally inclusive and principles-based multilateral framework for AI risk management, backed by independent and credible oversight,” Guterres said Monday. Guterres, who is approaching the end of his term due in December, has become increasingly vocal about the need for safety measures around advanced technology to avoid a future in which “ killer robots ” are a reality. Guterres said Monday at the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety that “when one looks at different other institutions of global governance … they correspond to the reality of the world in 1945”. “It’s clear that institutions need to be reformed in order to adapt themselves to the realities of today’s world,” he said. “That applies to the UN, and that applies to the international financial architecture, that applies to the world trade system.” Guterres said that he would advise his successor,

items.blurb: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the…
items.text: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press. Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war. items.headline: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
items.blurb: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.
items.text: Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't. The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi , co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders? The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch. Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes , has called it "a dangerous escalation". It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism. Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga. items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.headline: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
items.blurb: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.
items.text: King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness. Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning. The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba. Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry". Born in Victoria in 1943, Meldrum displayed a love of music from an early age and went on to host the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's music television programme Countdown, and later a segment on variety show Hey Hey, It's Saturday. Meldrum in 2014 became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame. Meldrum lived with an acquired brain injury after falling from a ladder in 2011.

The officials said that the suspects, identified as Rohtash and Dev, both residents of Faridabad, were arrested by the Sector 30 crime branch unit on Sunday. While Rohtash has been identified as a resident of Basel Colony, Dev is said to be a resident of Rajiv Nagar. According to police, the complainant, Avinash, a resident of Sector-29, told investigators that he had visited a hotel in Sector-31 with his family. “While reversing his car from the parking area after leaving the hotel, he accidentally ran over a dog,” Faridabad police public relations officer (PRO) Yashpal Yadav said. “This led to an argument with people present at the spot, who allegedly assaulted him. items.blurb: SEBI urged intermediaries and market participants to stop publishing grey market premium (GMP) figures for IPOs, warning that these unregulated estimates are unverified and cannot reliably predict listing prices or returns. Investors should avoid GMP-linked transactions and use authorised platforms.
items.text: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has stepped up its scrutiny of the unofficial grey market surrounding initial public offerings (IPOs), asking market intermediaries and participants to discontinue the publication and circulation of grey market premium (GMP) figures. In an advisory issued on Monday, 23 November, the market regulator cautioned investors against relying on GMP as an indication of an IPO's likely listing price or expected returns. It also advised investors to stay away from transactions linked to these unofficial premiums, which operate entirely outside the regulated securities market. The move comes amid the widespread circulation of IPO GMP figures across websites, digital platforms, newspapers and social media. These premiums are often followed by investors looking to gauge demand for an upcoming public issue and estimate its potential listing performance. SEBI said unregulated pre-listing premium figures, commonly referred to as grey market premiums, were being widely disseminated through multiple channels. It noted that some SEBI-registered intermediaries and market participants were also publishing such figures. items.text: Personal hygiene and wellness brand Pee Safe reported a 54% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in FY26. However, the company continued to remain in the red during the fiscal year. Pee Safe’s revenue from operations rose 53.7% to Rs 126 crore in FY26 from Rs 82 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). Founded by Vikas Bagaria and Srijana Bagaria, Pee Safe offers a range of personal hygiene and wellness products across categories such as menstrual care, intimate hygiene, toilet hygiene, sexual wellness, and grooming. Its product portfolio includes sanitary pads, menstrual cups, tampons, intimate washes, toilet seat sanitizers, lubricants and grooming products. Revenue from product sales remained the company's sole source of operating revenue, while it generated an additional Rs 1 crore through other income, taking its total income to Rs 127 crore in FY26. Advertising and promotional expenses, the largest cost component, surged 76.3% to Rs 46 crore in FY26 from Rs 26.09 crore in FY25, accounting for around 34% of total expenses. items.text: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team. The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. items.text: On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children. SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM). Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today. items.text: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well. Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm. This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll , 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.text: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack . You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey . You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit. items.text: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened. Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. items.blurb: Megaspeed, which was previously led by Alice Huang, would be barred from doing business with U.S. companies unless those companies attained a special license from the federal government.
items.text: Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday. The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.” Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.” Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. items.headline: Jensen Huang scheduled to testify next week in Senate following reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
items.blurb: The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about the affair with the suspected Chinese spy.
items.text: Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website. The development comes just hours after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, less than two weeks following his resignation after it was revealed that he engaged in at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by the U.S. government of working as a Chinese spy. The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries. The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations. It’s worth noting that before his reinstatement as CEO, Huang had already agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1.

IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures, and Tetration Ventures also joined the startup’s cap table, while existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners doubled down on their earlier bet on the Bengaluru-based AI startup. The startup will utilise the capital to accelerate R&D in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence, and prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents. items.headline: Sarvam AI Defends Token Factory, Says Homegrown Models Remain Core Focus
items.blurb: AI unicorn Sarvam AI has defended its Token Factory business, saying the platform runs on privately procured GPUs rather than…
items.text: Sarvam AI cofounder Pratyush Kumar said that Token Factory runs on privately-procured GPUs, while state-subsidised compute was used to train its 105B model The clarification addresses questions over whether Sarvam is using public infrastructure to host foreign AI models and shifting its focus away from developing homegrown alternatives Sarvam also released an upgraded 105B model, with more releases planned across vision, speech, and edge AI AI unicorn Sarvam AI has defended its Token Factory business, saying the platform runs on privately procured GPUs rather than government-subsidised computing capacity, while reiterating that developing homegrown AI models remains its core focus. In a post on X, cofounder Pratyush Kumar addressed questions about the startup’s government support, its decision to host global open-weight models, and whether its expansion into inference infrastructure signals a shift away from building indigenous models. Notably, Token Factory’s launch had sparked online debates about Sarvam’s use of government subsidised compute capacity and its ability to anchor India’s indigenous AI ambitions. items.headline: India’s Inference Test, Scaler Founder’s New AI Bet & More
items.blurb: Inside The Business Of Inference Platforms Sarvam is entering its commercial era with Token Factory. By serving global AI models…
items.text: Sarvam is entering its commercial era with Token Factory. By serving global AI models on local GPUs with Rupee billing, Sarvam is now chasing usage-driven revenues. But critics are flaying the unicorn’s new AI inference stack for questionable economics and hosting Chinese models. Sovereignty Debate: Token Factory lets developers toggle between Sarvam 105B and open-weight models from DeepSeek, Kimi and Gemma 4 31B via a single API. Its inclusion of Chinese models sparked scrutiny after critics questioned whether subsidised GPUs under IndiaAI Mission were powering Token Factory. Sarvam clarified that it is using its own hardware for the service, but questions surrounding its unit economics remain. Utilisation Economics: Running a token factory on its own GPUs means Sarvam carries the cost of idle capacity. As such, utilisation, not volume, will determine whether the service makes money for the AI unicorn. The expiration of promotional rates (₹0.25 per million tokens) by 2026-end will also test whether developers, who arrive for cheap open models, will ultimately stay for Sarvam’s proprietary stack.
